A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-restoration and Max-Former research, despite v3's broader title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, pooling and token-mixing ablations, frequency analyses, and measurements of training time and memory consumption.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds Max-ResNet classification experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

M1.justification: v3 adds Max-ResNet, a limited convolutional adaptation that inserts Max-Pool into selected MS-ResNet residual blocks (Section 4.4, Appendix A.3, Figure 7). The existing Max-Former architecture, patch embedding, DWC/SSA token mixing, and membrane shortcuts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, CIFAR10-DVS, and DVS128 Gesture. Max-ResNet uses existing CIFAR tasks; it adds an architecture, not a dataset, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds KDSNN-ResNet-18 and MS-ResNet-18/34 to the new convolutional comparison in Table 5. It also adds SWformer-8-512 to the ImageNet comparison in Table 3. QKFormer* becoming MS-QKFormer* is only a rename.

E3.justification: ImageNet Mixup changes from 0.2 in v2 Table 5 to 0.25/0.4/0.8 in v3 Table 6; this is a revised reported setting, without evidence establishing reruns. The new ResNet comparison specifies four timesteps and two ResNet-18 block configurations.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds an architecture-generality analysis comparing MS-ResNet and Max-ResNet with matching block configurations and parameter counts. Existing patch-embedding and token-mixing ablations, residual-connection analyses, and GradCAM examples are retained, including the appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's new checklist explicitly acknowledges that error bars are omitted because of computational expense, but introduces no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 Table 5 newly reports Max-ResNet-18 CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 accuracies of 96.81%/81.54% and 97.17%/83.06%, alongside convolutional baseline results. Table 3 adds SWformer's 75.43% ImageNet accuracy and 5.08 mJ energy estimate. Existing Max-Former benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The LIF/IF transfer functions, firing-rate linearization, cascade argument, and energy derivations are retained. The added beta = 1 - 1/tau paragraph reparameterizes the existing decay term and explains its frequency dependence; it introduces no new proof or substantive formal result.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and contributions broaden the empirical message from Spiking Transformers to SNNs across architectures, adding a state-of-the-art Max-ResNet claim. The introduction also changes '30% energy savings' to '30% energy consumption,' which conflicts with the unchanged Table 3 values.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the convolutional results as evidence that frequency restoration matters regardless of architecture. Section 3.1 expands the explanation of membrane time constants and waveform-induced high frequencies. Existing limitations concerning manual frequency balancing and shortcut deployment are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 and Figure 7 document Max-ResNet's pooling placement. v3 updates the code-repository pointer to MaxFormer and replaces the appendix's upon-acceptance release promise with public-code instructions. The ImageNet Mixup documentation is also revised; existing hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations concerning dynamic token masking, knowledge distillation, and a diffusion-model survey, and replaces SpikeZip-TF with Adaptive Calibration. Research positioning expands to convolutional SNNs, while most prior-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract, introductory framing, selected theoretical explanations, and conclusion. It adds Section 4.4, Appendix A.3, acknowledgements, and a NeurIPS checklist, and separates visualization into its own appendix. Most existing technical and experimental prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the ResNet comparison table and architecture diagram, expands Table 3 with SWformer, and reflows existing figures and tables. The GradCAM figure is retained with updated comparator labeling and numbering; the existing visual analyses are not replaced.

improvement.justification: The new ResNet comparisons and implementation diagram provide useful evidence beyond the Transformer architectures evaluated in v2, while revised code instructions improve reproducibility information. These are limited gains: the central Max-Former evidence is unchanged, and v3 introduces an energy-claim inconsistency by saying '30% energy consumption' where Table 3 supports roughly 30% savings.
